title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries

reading.body:
Pizza Hut required franchisees to adopt Dragontail, an AI system managing delivery coordination. The system gave delivery drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, which caused them to batch orders and wait longer before pickup. This created delays that exceeded the 30-minute delivery window the franchisee had previously maintained, damaging customer satisfaction and sales.

The failure was in the system's design or deployment: it exposed information to an actor in the delivery process who used that visibility in ways that degraded overall performance. A human review of how the system would affect driver behavior before mandatory rollout could have caught this. The franchisee says they received inadequate training and support and that Pizza Hut did not exercise reasonable business judgment in requiring the system, though the lawsuit has not been resolved and damages are not established.

reports.title: Pizza Hut's AI system caused 'cascading' problems and $100M in damages, franchisee alleges in new suit
Pizza Hut franchisee says AI caused $100M in damages
Frustrated franchisee sues Pizza Hut over crappy kitchen AI
A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries

summary:
A Pizza Hut franchisee operating 111 restaurants across the Northeast filed a lawsuit on May 6 alleging that the chain's mandatory adoption of Dragontail, an AI-powered delivery management system, caused over 100 million dollars in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast claims the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, prompting them to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together. This delay prevented pizzas from arriving within the previously reliable 30-minute window, frustrated customers, and tanked sales and satisfaction scores that had previously exceeded system averages.

The franchisee argues Pizza Hut breached their franchise agreement by requiring continued use of the faulty software without adequate training or support and without exercising reasonable business judgment. Chaac reported that year-over-year sales growth in New York City fell from positive 10.19 percent to negative 9.78 percent following the rollout. The company is seeking over 100 million dollars in damages plus attorney fees and additional relief. Pizza Hut said it would respond through appropriate legal channels but declined further comment.
